pharm: Preferentially stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, activating adenyl cyclase to relax bronchial smooth muscle and relieve bronchospasm
quick: 5 mg orally three times daily at ~6-hour intervals; max 15 mg/24 h (reduce to 2.5 mg TID if side effects)
May be taken with or without food
Category C; NOT for tocolysis - serious maternal/fetal harm and death reported
Excretion into milk unknown; use only if benefit justifies risk to newborn
Use with caution; no specific oral adjustment stated in labeling
No specific adjustment stated in labeling
Heart rate, blood pressure, serum potassium, blood glucose, asthma control
summary: Terbutaline sulfate is a selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist (bronchodilator) indicated for the prevention and reversal of bronchospasm in patients 12 years and older with asthma and reversible bronchospasm associated with bronchitis and emphysema. Oral tablets are given three times daily. It carries a boxed warning that oral terbutaline is not approved and should not be used for tocolysis because of serious maternal adverse reactions, including death.
indications: Prevention and reversal of bronchospasm in patients >=12 years with asthma
Reversible bronchospasm associated with bronchitis and emphysema

dosage.d: 5 mg orally at approximately 6-hour intervals, three times daily during waking hours
dosage.t: Three times daily; total dose within 24 h should not exceed 15 mg
dosage.n: If side effects are disturbing, reduce to 2.5 mg three times daily

dosage.t: Three times daily; total within 24 h should not exceed 7.5 mg
dosage.n: Not recommended below 12 years of age

admin: Administer orally as tablets, spaced at approximately 6-hour intervals during waking hours
Do not exceed 15 mg in 24 hours (adults) or 7.5 mg in 24 hours (12-15 years)
Reduce the dose to 2.5 mg three times daily if side effects are disturbing
Seek medical advice if a previously effective regimen fails to relieve symptoms (sign of worsening asthma)
Do NOT use oral terbutaline for tocolysis (boxed warning)
moa: Terbutaline exerts a preferential effect on beta-2 adrenergic receptors. The pharmacologic effects of beta-adrenergic agonists are at least in part attributable to stimulation through beta-adrenergic receptors of intracellular adenyl cyclase, increasing cyclic AMP, which relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and inhibits release of mediators of immediate hypersensitivity. Although there is relative beta-2 selectivity, beta-1 (cardiac) effects can occur, and beta-2 receptors are also present in the human heart.

absolute: Use for acute or maintenance tocolysis (oral terbutaline - boxed warning)
Hypersensitivity to sympathomimetic amines or any component of the product
relative: Cardiovascular disorders (ischemic heart disease, hypertension, arrhythmias)
monitor: Heart rate, blood pressure, and ECG changes

preg: Pregnancy Category C. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Oral terbutaline has not been approved and should not be used for tocolysis - serious adverse reactions including death have been reported after administration to pregnant women (maternal tachycardia, transient hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, myocardial ischemia), and increased fetal heart rate and neonatal hypoglycemia may occur. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: It is not known whether terbutaline is excreted in human milk. Therefore terbutaline sulfate should be used during nursing only if the potential benefit justifies the possible risk to the newborn.
renal: No specific oral dose adjustment is described in the labeling; use with caution as with other sympathomimetics.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described in the labeling.

major: Other sympathomimetic agents - combined cardiovascular effects may be deleterious (concomitant use not recommended, except an adrenergic aerosol bronchodilator for acute bronchospasm)
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors / tricyclic antidepressants - may potentiate cardiovascular effects
Non-cardioselective beta-blockers - may block bronchodilation and cause severe bronchospasm
moderate: Potassium-depleting agents (e.g. loop/thiazide diuretics, corticosteroids) - additive hypokalemia
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, and ECG changes that affect laboratory/ECG interpretation

serious: Clinically significant cardiovascular effects (arrhythmias, marked tachycardia, blood pressure changes)
Aggravation of diabetes and ketoacidosis (with large IV doses)

monitoring: Heart rate and rhythm; blood pressure
Asthma control and frequency of use (increasing need signals destabilization)
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and do not exceed the daily limit
If you need this medicine more often than usual, your asthma may be worsening - contact your clinician promptly
Tremor, nervousness, headache, and a faster heartbeat are common and usually lessen with continued use
Tell your clinician about heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid problems, diabetes, or seizures
This medicine is not for stopping premature labor
pk: Bronchodilation typically within ~30 minutes of an oral dose
Peak plasma concentration about 1.5 to 2 hours after an oral dose
Elimination half-life approximately 3.4 hours in asthmatic patients
Action lasts up to 6 hours or longer; oral bioavailability variable (partly excreted in feces)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); dispense in a tight, light-resistant container with child-resistant closure
pearls: Selective beta-2 agonist bronchodilator - relative, not absolute, cardiac sparing (beta-1 effects still occur)
Boxed warning: oral terbutaline must NOT be used for tocolysis - maternal deaths and serious cardiovascular events reported
Increasing need for terbutaline is a marker of destabilizing asthma - reassess and add/optimize inhaled corticosteroids
Can cause hypokalemia and hyperglycemia - relevant in diabetics and with potassium-depleting drugs
Avoid non-selective beta-blockers, which can block bronchodilation and provoke severe bronchospasm
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose or exceed the maximum daily amount (15 mg/day in adults).
overdose: Overdose produces exaggerated beta-adrenergic stimulation: seizures, angina, hypertension or hypotension, tachycardia up to 200 beats/min, arrhythmias, nervousness, headache, tremor, dry mouth, palpitation, nausea, dizziness, fatigue, malaise, insomnia, and hypokalemia. There is no specific antidote; treatment consists of discontinuing terbutaline with appropriate symptomatic and supportive care. Judicious use of a cardioselective beta-receptor blocker may be considered, recognizing it can provoke bronchospasm. Monitor cardiac status.
